root_idea.summary: The root centers on remaining firmly established, especially settling or kneeling, and develops toward the idea of good that is firmly established, increasing, and abundant.
root_idea.development: The physical image is a camel settling on its breast or remaining at a place. From this come terms for a place where water remains and for enduring or increasing divine good; the Quranic Form VI further applies this development to divine abundance and exaltation.

senses.definition: To bless; to confer or perpetuate enduring, increasing, or abundant good upon someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran this is a transitive Form III use with people, places, things, and natural phenomena as its objects. Related blessing constructions use في, لِ, or عَلَى; in blessing formulas the expression may function as a prayer for such good.

senses.definition: To be abundant and enduring in good; to be the source of overflowing blessing.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage this is an invariable divine predicate, associated with the abundance, continuation, and exclusive bestowal of the good mentioned in the surrounding passage.

senses.definition: To be exalted, glorified, hallowed, and far above every imperfection or limitation.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a Quranic divine expression of magnification and exaltation, not an ordinary reciprocal or general-purpose Form VI verb.

senses.definition: Blessing or divinely bestowed good that is firmly established, continues, increases, and abounds; blessings, prosperity, or beneficial abundance.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural بَرَكَات denotes such continuing or increasing divine good bestowed from or upon a place, people, or thing.

senses.definition: Blessed; possessing, containing, or transmitting firmly established and increasing divine good, benefit, or utility.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran applies the form adjectivally and substantively to persons, places, times, revelation, water, and other things in which such divine good is present or from which it proceeds. The feminine form is included under this citation form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kneel or lie down upon the breast; of a camel and, by extension, other beings, to settle in this posture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same physical posture is used of a camel, ostrich, lion, or man; in prayer it refers to descending with the hands before the knees in the camel-like manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become firm, settled, steadfast, or fixed; to remain or stay in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or thing that holds its position, including the expression for standing firm for battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the night, to become long or protracted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension treating the night as though it did not leave its place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pray for or invoke blessing on a person, food, or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes formulas meaning “God bless you” or invoking blessing on food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply oneself constantly or perseveringly to an affair, commerce, or traffic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical Form III use distinct from its Quranic blessing sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a camel kneel or lie down upon its breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative action may be expressed in a sequence where the camel is made to kneel and then kneels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا أَبْرَكَهُ, to be extraordinarily blessed: “How blessed is he or it!”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional verb of wonder with passive meaning and an irregular derivation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or derive blessing through a person, thing, or utterance; to regard it as a means of obtaining blessing or as an auspicious sign.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِهِ, بِالشَّيْءِ, and in expressions such as تَبَرَّكْ بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw one’s breast upon the ground or upon another thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily action modeled on the camel’s breast-first settling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lean or bear upon something; of a horse, to incline to one side while running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person leaning on a polishing instrument and of a horse’s movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten, speed, and exert oneself in running; to strive or labour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated verbal noun may denote strenuous exertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud or the sky, to rain continually, heavily, or vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of forceful settling or bearing down upon the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To detract from someone’s reputation, censure or impugn his character, and revile him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي or عَلَى in the expression for labouring in vituperation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In war, to fall upon the knees and fight one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The combatants are described as kneeling in battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prostrate another person, throw him down, and place him beneath one’s breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive physical use derived from the breast-first posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large herd or collective of camels, especially camels lying upon their breasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote the camels of an encampment returning from pasture, whether few or very numerous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The breast or chest, primarily of a camel; by extension, the corresponding breast area of other animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical descriptions distinguish the interior, exterior, middle, or lower skin area of the breast; these are anatomical specifications of the same lexical branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first or main part of winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative temporal extension from remaining or settling in place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the stars composing the Scorpion constellation, or for a related stellar station associated with the period when camels lie down from cold and rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional astronomical and seasonal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remaining fixed at or beside a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in an idiomatic description of someone remaining beside a vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An incubus or nightmare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare figurative or technical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare figurative use, also applied to a related form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ancient name for the month Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A historical calendrical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain small white aquatic bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term has also been applied to a duck in later regional usage; the classical meaning is the bird designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The manner or mode in which a camel kneels and lies upon its breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of manner corresponding to the act of kneeling or settling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A watering-trough, tank, basin, pool, or other place where water remains, collects, or stagnates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classically it may be dug into the ground without raised sides and may designate constructed cisterns as well as natural or collected water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: “Be firm, steady, or steadfast,” especially in battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed battle expression equivalent in force to a command to kneel or hold one’s ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who marries while already having a large son of pubescent age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare conventional social description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hastening, speeding, striving, or exerting oneself in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated with the Form VIII running sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Kneeling or lying upon the breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of بَرَكَ in its physical settling sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmness, steadfastness, and strenuous exertion in battle; kneeling and fighting in combat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the condition or action of combatants who hold their ground or fight from the knees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The field of battle, especially the place to which valiant men cleave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional place-name extension of battle steadfastness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well-known woollen cloak or wrap, especially a black garment with ornamental borders.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry records several variant forms and plurals for this garment term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A substance put into flour or dough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare food-preparation term, defined by cross-reference to بُورَقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where camels lie upon their breasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is مَبَارِكُ; the term may be used idiomatically for possession of a camel or camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leaning or bearing upon something and applying oneself to it perseveringly, assiduously, or constantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a person’s sustained application to an object or task.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud, bearing down upon the earth and forcefully stripping or paring its surface with rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of vehement rainfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: High or exalted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Apparently applied to God and understood through the corresponding divine verb.
